item.text:
## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Before merge, make refresh preserve stored fingerprints so verification can still detect edits to tracked files.

## Changes

The pull request adds two helpers for updating the integrity manifest and tests for adding new files and preserving existing fingerprints.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve existing fingerprints during refresh — Passing `["tracked.txt", "new.txt"]` to refresh after editing `tracked.txt` makes `verify` accept the edit. The unconditional assignment replaces the saved fingerprint with the digest of the edited contents. — Users can lose the baseline for detecting edits to tracked files while adding new files to the manifest. — Fix: Have `refresh_fingerprints` reuse `register_new_files` and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries`.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:25 — correctness — Reject the manifest itself as an input file — When `fingerprints.json` is an unlisted file under the content root, passing its name to either helper creates an entry that immediately fails verification. Both helpers hash the manifest before adding that entry to it. — A batch that includes the manifest leaves verification failing even when every other tracked file matches its saved fingerprint.
